property_summary: For any inputs to initialize(...), the reference contract sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken (so c.baseToken() == _baseToken after a successful initialize), whereas the mutant sets baseToken to address(0) breaking this equality for inputs where _baseToken != address(0).

For every initialize(...) call, the contract's public baseToken getter equals the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant sets baseToken to the factory instead, breaking this rule for inputs where _baseToken != factory.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken argument; the mutant sets baseToken equal to _nft instead, so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken (mutant) while in the reference c.baseToken() == _baseToken for all inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public nft() getter returns the exact _nft address passed to initialize (reference preserves this invariant); the mutant that sets nft = address(0) breaks this for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed C contract's nft state variable equals the _nft argument passed (i.e. nft() == _nft); the mutant sets nft to msg.sender breaking this rule for calls where msg.sender != _nft.
